perItemFindings.one_line: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; directed reroute: Strengthen the existential thirty-two-type refinement certificate into a characterization of when both endpoints strictly improve for the general finite SLCC incidence model, and prove that the characterized region is nonempty and relatively open under primitive design conditions.

review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The general sharp-interval claim is obtained by encoding the note's finite SCM class as a response-type simplex, so its substantive identification content beyond the generic discrete-response framework is concentrated in the specialized thirty-two-type construction. The proved strict benefit of revealed labels is existential: it covers one singleton-stratum, two-trial-arm, common-recommendation design and a neighborhood of one constructed law, not a characterization across the advertised finite multi-policy class. The atomic-tie inference theorem is conditional on local finite-fan exactness and a law-dependent slack dominating an unspecified approximation error, while its concrete witness has the degenerate limit H(G)=0 and therefore does not demonstrate nontrivial atomic-quantile behavior. Thus the broad sharp-bounds framing exceeds the breadth of the new explicit result, although the text does not falsely claim uniform inference or tightness for the published Zhang–Skalnes–Chen–Oberst class.

DIRECTED IMPROVEMENT (re-derive the SAME object implementing this, do not reproduce the prior note): Strengthen the existential thirty-two-type refinement certificate into a characterization of when both endpoints strictly improve for the general finite SLCC incidence model, and prove that the characterized region is nonempty and relatively open under primitive design conditions.

Verify it on a simultaneous projection/LP tie whose limiting statistic has a genuinely nondegenerate atom, rather than the displayed case where H(G) is identically zero.

review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note proves sharp LP endpoints for its finite SLCC class and a stable two-sided improvement witness, but the sharpness argument is largely the standard finite response-function construction specialized to a newly defined observation model. The arbitrary-design dual-face equivalence is an LP-duality restatement; the substantive design result remains only the bracket-stratum sufficient family and its thirty-two-type certificate, not a primitive characterization. The advertised atomic-tie inference is under-delivered because its theorem requires a law-dependent approximation error and an unknown slack schedule, while its sole boundary certificate has H(G) identically zero rather than a nondegenerate atomic limit. The TL;DR and honest-scope sections call atomic tie-inclusive subsampling validity open even though a later theorem presents conditional validity as established, leaving the framing internally inconsistent about what has actually been settled.

DIRECTED IMPROVEMENT (re-derive the SAME object implementing this, do not reproduce the prior note): Strengthen the subsampling theorem by replacing the unknown, law-dependent approximation error and slack-dominance requirement with an explicit feasible rate or data-driven choice of slack and subsample size. Verify it on a simultaneous projection/LP tie whose limiting statistic has a genuinely nondegenerate atom, rather than the displayed case where H(G) is identically zero.
